title: Compatibility of quantum instruments
authors: Chloe Kim, Yujie Zhang, Eric Chitambar, Marius Junge, Felix Leditzky
abstract: Measurement compatibility asks whether a family of quantum measurements can be simulated by one parent measurement followed by classical post-processing. We extend this measurement compatibility to the notion of \emph{$d$-compatibility} for measurements, channels, and instruments whose parent passes a $d$-dimensional quantum system and unlimited classical information to the post-processing. We formulate $d$-compatibility as a common linear factorization of operator spaces and operator systems and show that $d$-compatible families form a closed set, even with infinitely many settings and a separable infinite-dimensional input. To certify $d$-incompatibility, we define the compatibility functional as the smallest product of completely bounded norms over common factorizations through a $d$-dimensional register. Using factorization theory of operator spaces, we show that measure-and-prepare channels defined in terms of mutually unbiased bases and pinching channels defined in terms of Heisenberg-Weyl operators are $d$-incompatible in certain regimes of $d$. We also link $d$-compatibility of multi-instruments to the preparability of Choi assemblages using channel-state duality, and use this connection to show that for bipartite states the (in)compatibility of instruments can be used to certify Schmidt numbers and the implementability of the instrument using one-way LOCC protocols. Finally, our compatibility functional also bounds the generalized robustness of compatibility, which we interpret through a memory-bounded nontransient preparation game.
summary: This work develops a generalized concept called $d$-compatibility to characterize when a set of quantum measurements or instruments can be simulated by a single parent measurement using limited quantum memory ($d$ dimensions). By translating this into a problem of linear factorization in operator spaces, the authors provide powerful, mathematically rigorous tools to quantify the resource cost of quantum information processing.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum measurement compatibility, asking whether a family of measurements can be simulated by a single 'parent' measurement followed by classical post-processing.
main_result: It extends this concept to '$d$-compatibility' using operator factorization, establishing that compatible families form closed sets and providing a functional to certify incompatibility.
method: The core method involves reformulating compatibility into a problem of linear factorization within the language of operator spaces and operator systems.
model_or_system: The study applies to general quantum measurements, multi-instruments, and quantum channels, generalizing the concept to include a $d$-dimensional quantum memory resource.
key_observables: Measurement compatibility, $d$-compatibility, Schmidt numbers, and generalized robustness of compatibility.
important_parameters: The dimension parameter $d$, which quantifies the required quantum memory resource for simulation.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on advanced functional analysis theorems concerning operator spaces and the structure of completely bounded maps.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates a circuit diagram representing a $d$-compatible multi-instrument, showing the flow through quantum and classical processing lines.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the definition of compatibility to the generalized $d$-compatibility, develops the mathematical machinery using operator factorization, and applies these tools to certify incompatibility for specific physical models.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting measurement compatibility to operator factorization provides powerful tools for quantifying the resource cost (quantum memory $d$) required to simulate complex quantum operations.
